statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON; Tail is low while FOMC event Stress is extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON; the FOMC decision/press conference is the main near-term checkpoint.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress into the FOMC
body: Nasdaq equities were higher with positive breadth while oil and the 10-year yield eased. Strong retail-sales and import-price data keep rates sensitivity high. Live NQ retracement structure is not independently verified, so event proximity alone does not establish a persistent no-retracement path.

lookbackSummary: Prior-24h Tail moved from WATCH late September 15 to low overnight, briefly returned to WATCH around September 16 U.S. data/open, then returned to 19% by 16:00 UTC. Stress stayed extreme.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail peaks around the 18:00 UTC FOMC decision, 18:30 press conference and possible delayed second leg into the close. It should decay if trade turns two-way. The next scheduled U.S. cluster is 12:30 UTC September 17.

forecast.analysis: Nasdaq was 0.78% higher at 15:46 UTC with positive breadth; oil and the 10-year yield were lower. Live NQ retracement structure is unverified. FOMC proximity keeps Stress extreme; Tail is 19% low.

news.title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 climb as oil retreat tempers pre-Fed jitters
Robust US retail sales underscore economy's resilience; inflation pressures building
US import prices jump in August on strength in capital, consumer goods

forecast.analysis: The 18:00 UTC FOMC decision and 18:30 press conference make this the peak event hour. Tail is 24% WATCH conditionally; persistent extension or failed pullbacks would be escalation evidence.
Press-conference/Q&A overlaps the U.S. power hour. Tail stays 24% WATCH unless price discovery becomes persistently one-way rather than two-way and retracing.
The cash-close transition can carry a delayed policy second leg. Tail is 23% WATCH; absent continued extension or failed retracements, risk should start decaying after the close.
Post-FOMC after-hours trade should separate event impulse from ordinary volatility. Tail is 20% WATCH only if the move keeps extending with poor retracement.
If futures become two-way and cross-assets stabilize, Tail falls to 18% low. Stress stays high because policy repricing can still transmit into Asia.
Asia tests whether the Fed move is reinforced or retraced. Without sustained directional efficiency, Tail remains 17% low as Stress eases.
Balanced overnight trade keeps Tail at 17% low. A renewed rates-led extension would invalidate normalization and raise the next-hour path.
Two-way overnight trade supports 17% low Tail. A fresh geopolitical or rates discontinuity would be the main path back toward WATCH.
Late-Asia Tail is 17% low if no delayed policy leg appears. Holding near an extreme with repeated failed retracements would lift risk into Europe.
Europe can reprice the Fed through rates, FX and global tech. Tail stays 18% low unless cross-assets align with persistent NQ extension.
European follow-through may confirm or fade the overnight move. A clean fade supports 18% low Tail; shallow-pullback extension would lift risk.
U.S. premarket focus increases. Tail remains 18% low unless a second persistent Fed leg emerges with yield pressure and aligned tech weakness.
Premarket positioning can amplify the prior move, but Tail is 18% low without repeated extension. The 12:30 UTC data cluster becomes the next checkpoint.
Residual Fed sensitivity remains before tomorrow's data. Tail is 18% low unless pre-release structure is already directional and poorly retracing.
The 12:30 UTC housing, claims and Philadelphia Fed cluster approaches. Stress rises; Tail is 19% low unless data trigger persistent one-way rates/NQ repricing.
drivers: Housing, claims and Philly Fed at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: The first post-data hour overlaps the U.S. cash-open transition. Tail is 20% WATCH conditionally if opening-auction extension is sustained with shallow pullbacks.
The first full post-open hour remains 20% WATCH if the data/open impulse keeps extending. A meaningful retracement or cross-asset divergence would reduce Tail.
By midmorning, Tail falls to 19% low if two-way trade returns. Persistent session-extreme holding with failed pullbacks is the main contrary signal.
Later-morning Tail is 18% low if the opening move retraces. Continued one-way extension would keep Stress elevated and prevent expected risk decay.
Absent a new catalyst, midday Tail is 18% low. A renewed directional rates impulse that keeps NQ near an extreme would invalidate the baseline.
Two-way midday trade keeps Tail at 18% low. Unusually efficient one-direction price action with repeated failed pullbacks would lift it.
With no scheduled Tier-1 U.S. event in this hour, Tail is 18% low. Geopolitical headlines or bond repricing are the main unscheduled escalation paths.
Later-session Tail stays 18% low under balanced trade. Fresh extension linked to rates, technology breadth or geopolitics would move the state toward WATCH.
